bear.argument: The bull's own numbers undercut the add. OIL is the only line he would move, yet its 10-day momentum is -3.41% and its 1-day move is +1.00 sigma with 46.7% annualized vol: he is buying a pullback in the most volatile line on the book, paying 18 bps/side plus 0.96 bps/day carry, on a news card that explicitly says the gas/propane records are not a crude supply story (K:news:3) and that the 'higher oil' headline carries no shock (K:news:1). Everything else is frozen, so the honest bear case is: hold the reference, add nothing. The rate move is not absorbed, it is recent: DGS10 +50 bps in 20 days to 5.29%, DGS2 +49 bps, DFF +25 bps, dollar +1.67% in 20 days. SPX sits only +0.32% over its SMA50 with mom10d +0.43% - the trend is intact but flat, and the 2% hysteresis means a small slip flips it to mixed. GOLD is the real damage: -22.82% off its high, -8.04% below SMA200, mom10d -3.92%.

claims.text: OIL's add case fails on its own evidence: mom10d -3.41%, ret1d_sigma +1.00, sigma_ann 46.67%, and the news cards say the supply headlines are gas/NGL, not crude.
The rate shock is fresh, not absorbed: DGS10 +50 bps in 20 days to 5.29%, DGS2 +49 bps, DFF +25 bps, and the trade-weighted dollar +1.67% in 20 days.
SPX is the weakest 'uptrend' on the book: only +0.32% over SMA50, mom10d +0.43%, mom63d +2.83%. With 2% hysteresis, a modest slip flips it to mixed and the reference drops to 0.75.
GOLD is in a confirmed downtrend: -8.04% below SMA200, -3.37% below SMA50, mom10d -3.92%, dd52 -22.82%. The reference 0.25 is already the floor; nothing here argues for more.
EURUSD printed a -2.42 sigma day with vol shock 1.54x, the largest single-line shock in the pack; the band pins it at 0.00, which is the correct outcome, not a missed trade.
Crypto is reference-only at 110 bps/side, and both BTC and ETH have negative 10-day momentum (-2.01%, -2.51%) with dd52 -31.91% and -42.22%; no deviation is available or warranted.

bull.argument: Every equity line is in an uptrend and the reference already holds it at full size: NDX +3.8% over SMA50 and +11.3% over SMA200 with mom63d +4.2% and dd52 only -0.7%; SEMIS +9.0%/+27.2% with mom10d +11.0%; SPX +0.3%/+6.6% with vol 0.80x of its 1y median. All three are frozen at their current levels, so the honest bull case is simply: hold, pay nothing, and let the trend work. The strongest bearish fact is the 20-day rate move (M:DGS10.chg20 +50 bps to 5.29%), but equities have already absorbed it while sitting within 1.5% of their 52-week highs, and VIX at 16.39 is not a stress reading. The only add I would argue is OIL, where the band opens to +0.50 and the trend is up +30.7% over SMA200; the 10-day -3.4% pullback is the entry, not the thesis. GBPUSD's band also allows an add but its price is below both averages, so I decline it.

rebuttal.argument: The bear's best point is OIL's entry cost, and I take it: 18 bps/side plus 0.96 bps/day carry against ret1d_sigma +1.00 and mom10d -3.41% is not a cheap entry, and K:news:3 confirms the gas/propane records are not a crude supply story. I therefore withdraw the OIL add and move to reference everywhere. But the bear's rate claim is not a measurement of equity damage: DGS10 +50 bps is real, yet NDX dd52 is -0.73%, SEMIS -11.96%, SPX -1.54%, and VIX 16.39 - the shock is in yields, not in equity prices.
